---
title: "Research"
pagetitle: "Research - Kamil Gacek"
description-meta: "Environmentally extended Input-Output modelling, water footprint analysis and disaster impact assessment for the Polish economy."
page-layout: article
---

Input-Output models describe an economy as a web of mutual supplies: every sector's output is
another sector's input, so a change in one place is never confined to it. I work with the
environmentally extended version of that framework, in which a physical quantity - water above all
- travels alongside the monetary flows. That makes it possible to ask how much of a resource an
activity uses directly and how much it draws through everything it buys, to decompose a change in
resource use into the forces behind it, and to follow a disruption as it spreads through the
structure of production. The computation is done in R, on national supply-and-use and Input-Output
tables combined with environmental accounts. The reason for working this way is that the damage
from a physical shortage is mostly indirect, and indirect damage tends to go uncounted: it is
assessed once the season is over, sector by sector, and whatever cannot be traced drops out of the
total. A model of the dependencies makes that part visible in advance. The longer-term aim is a
usable tool: a model in which a disruption can be simulated and mitigation strategies compared
before a drought, rather than accounted for after one.
